blocking.issue: The replica join flow cannot work in the order this document gives. `ruralz control join` runs before `ruralz control serve`, so nothing on the new host answers Raft traffic on 8092 when the leader handles `Join`. Control plane and GitOps says the leader "signs the replica's certificate and adds a voter" in that same step. With hashicorp/raft, adding a voter that is not running raises the quorum at once. On the common 1-to-3 bootstrap, a 1-voter cluster becomes 2 voters with one down: the leader loses its lease and writes, logins and Enrollment stop (RZ-CP-004) until `serve` starts. The command also has no flag for the new replica's own advertised peer address (HOST:8092). The leader needs that address to add the server, and the peer certificate needs it as a SAN for mTLS on 8092. Finally, the document does not say how `ruralz control serve` on a data directory written by `join` knows not to bootstrap a new cluster and generate new CAs, which is what it does on an empty Control Store.
blocking.evidence: "`ruralz control join` runs on the new replica's host before `ruralz control serve`. It generates the key pair in `--data-dir`, dials `--peer` pinned to the SHA-256 fingerprint of the 8092 server CA ... then writes the certificate chain and peer CA beside the key"; command row: "| `ruralz control join` | Join a new replica to Raft | `--data-dir PATH`, `--peer HOST:8092`, `--join-token-file PATH` |"; Control plane and GitOps: "`ruralz control serve` on an empty Control Store generates the CAs or loads supplied ones; `ruralz control join` redeems a one-time `admin` token in `Join`, and the leader signs the replica's certificate and adds a voter."
blocking.fix: Add `--advertise HOST:8092` (required) to `ruralz control join`, and put that address into the certificate request as a SAN. State that `Join` only issues the certificate and records a pending member. The replica is added as a non-voter only when `ruralz control serve` on that data directory first connects over 8092 with its new peer certificate. It is promoted to voter only after it catches up to the leader's commit index (hashicorp/raft AddNonvoter, then AddVoter). State that `serve` on a joined data directory never bootstraps or generates CAs. Record the voter-timing change as a proposal to Control plane and GitOps, in OQ-cli-and-api-surface-9 or a new Open question owned by control-plane-and-gitops. The other option is to make join a mode of serve (`ruralz control serve -- --join HOST:8092 --join-token-file PATH --advertise HOST:8092`), so the replica is running before it becomes a member.

blocking.issue: `ruralz control restore` does not say what happens to Raft membership. A Raft snapshot carries the old cluster configuration: the old voters' IDs and addresses. Restored into an empty deployment on new hosts, that configuration leaves the new replica waiting for voters that no longer exist. It never elects a leader, so it can never open the higher `storeEpoch`. Neither restore step takes the local replica's advertised peer address, and neither step resets membership.
blocking.evidence: "2. `FILE --data-dir PATH --anchor-set PATH --backup-key-file PATH` verifies and decrypts the backup, requires a root-signed anchor set holding the prepared key, and opens a higher `storeEpoch` before any delivery."; Control plane and GitOps: "`ruralz control backup` writes a Raft snapshot plus referenced content, consistent at one index"
blocking.fix: Add `--advertise HOST:8092` (required) to step 2. State that restore replaces the snapshot's Raft configuration with a single voter: the local replica at that address, with a new server ID, as hashicorp/raft RecoverCluster does. It also clears old peer certificates from the trust set. Other replicas then join with `ruralz control join` (L1-1). If the Control plane document should own this, add it to OQ-cli-and-api-surface-9, or open a new Open question owned by control-plane-and-gitops.

non_blocking.suggestion: Held revert (OQ-cli-and-api-surface-8, option a): say whether a `pending` revert waiting for approval counts as the Cluster's active Rollout, which would block every promotion with RZ-CP-009 until someone decides. Also say when its per-Node plan is computed: pack 8.3 records the plan at `pending`, and a revert held for hours would carry a stale member list. Suggest computing the plan at approval and adding a hold expiry (target). Control plane and GitOps currently says "A Rollout exists only after approval", so keep option (a) clearly marked as proposed until that document changes.

`--api-version` conversion of overlay files: Configuration model says "the converter writes a field explicitly whenever the source version's default differs from the target's". Applied to a standalone overlay patch, that rule would clobber base values. State that overlays are converted as patches (only fields present) and defaults are made explicit only in base files; otherwise the empty-diff check will reject many real Bundles.

Ephemeral ports: picking free ports in the CLI and then handing them to `ruralzd` is a race between the check and the bind. State that a bind failure triggers one re-pick and relaunch before exit 2. Also state that `ruralz dev run --ephemeral-ports` keeps the same mapping across re-renders, so Hot Reload does not move listeners.

Local ruralzd: security and identity rule 5 refuses to start when `RURALZ_SECRET_ROOT` contains `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}` or an admin token file. State that the CLI puts the secret root, the temporary data directory and the admin token file in three separate subdirectories of its private directory.

`ruralz node drain`: `/proc/locks` reports PID -1 for open file description (OFD) locks. Say, in OQ-cli-and-api-surface-10, that the check assumes `flock` or POSIX record locks, or rely only on the PID and start-time record plus a non-blocking lock probe.

`ruralz test run --bundle` against a TLS listener needs the test client to trust the certificate supplied through `--secret-overrides`, and to know which listener a case targets. Name both in OQ-cli-and-api-surface-13 (for example `tls.caFile` and `listener`).
